project.name: Sample Classpath Matrix
project.description:
Proves that the stub runner's embedded WireMock actually starts and serves under every runtime we claim to support, rather than only resolving on paper.
This exists because of stubborn-sh/stubborn#142: WireMock's wiremock-jetty12 brings jetty-ee10 12.0.x, while Spring Boot 4.1 aligns Jetty core to 12.1.x and imports jetty-ee11-bom. Those load together and the stub server dies with
NoSuchMethodError: org.eclipse.jetty.util.component.Environment.ensure(String)
Pinning the core down to 12.0.x is NOT the fix - that is what broke spring-boot-starter-jetty applications in the first place. There are two real fixes. Align ee10 with the Jetty Boot already manages (12.1.x publishes ee10, and wiremock-jetty12 runs on it) - that is what Stubborn's BOM does from 0.2.1 on, and what sample-jetty-alignment demonstrates. Or stop sharing a Jetty at all, which is what the modules below do: wiremock-standalone is shaded, carrying its Jetty relocated under wiremock.org.eclipse.jetty, so the application and the stub server each get their own and cannot collide. Shading costs you Stubborn's response-template helpers, because it relocates Handlebars too, so prefer alignment unless you need a stub server that cannot be perturbed by the application's Jetty at all.
Each module below asserts both halves: the application's own Jetty is whatever its framework manages, AND a stub server boots and serves a request on the same JVM.
